LLR2 drift detector

Source: R/dfr_llr2.R
dfr_llr2.Rd

Fully unsupervised drift detector of Sojo, Bielza and Larrañaga (2027). A semiparametric Bayesian network (spbn()) is learned on a baseline of the stream. For every node i, the statistic Lambda_i = mean log f(x_i | pa_i) over the most recent sliding window minus the same mean over a fixed reference window is compared with the chi-square distribution with one degree of freedom, p_i = 1 - F(2 |Lambda_i|); a drift is reported when some p_i < alpha (or, with fdr = TRUE, when the Benjamini-Hochberg procedure rejects some node at level alpha: LLR2-BH). The nodes that drift are reported, and the network is updated.

Usage

dfr_llr2(
  target_feat = NULL,
  n_baseline = 4096,
  window_size = 250,
  step = 50,
  alpha = 0.05,
  fdr = FALSE,
  update = c("parameter", "parameter_sliding", "sliding", "none"),
  structure = NULL,
  node_types = NULL,
  max_parents = 4,
  folds = 5
)

Arguments

target_feat

Names of the columns to be monitored. NULL (the default) monitors every numeric column.

n_baseline

Size of the baseline: the first n_baseline - window_size observations learn the network (W_l) and the last window_size form the reference window (W_r).

window_size

Size of the sliding and reference windows (n_samples in the paper).

step

Stride of the sliding window: the test is run on observations whose position in the stream is a multiple of step.

alpha

Significance level.

fdr

TRUE for the Benjamini-Hochberg correction across nodes (LLR2-BH).

update

Update after a drift: "parameter" (default; the CPDs become the weighted geometric mean of CPDs fitted on the sliding window and on the learning window, Eq. 11-13), "parameter_sliding" (CPDs refitted on the sliding window), "sliding" (structure and CPDs learned again on the sliding window) or "none".

structure, node_types, max_parents, folds

Passed to spbn() for the baseline network.

Value

dfr_llr2 object. After fit(), drifter_output holds, for every observation, its log-likelihood under the network in use (loglik) and, on tested observations, the p-value of every node (p_<node>); obj$drifts lists the drifts with their nodes, and obj$network the current network.

Details

After a drift the reference window is emptied; the first full sliding window after the drift becomes the new reference window (its mean log-likelihood under the updated network) and tests resume at the next stride. This reproduces the spacing of the detections of the reference results (at least window_size + step observations between two drifts).

The "parameter" update follows Section 4.3: for every node, the CPD fitted on the sliding window (target, weight eta = window_size / |W_l|) is combined with the CPD fitted on the learning window (source, weight 1 - eta); if the risk |L_T| - |L_S| (cross-validated log-likelihood of the sliding window under the target CPD against its log-likelihood under the source) is not positive, the source is dropped (eta = 1). The structure is kept; the paper also relearns the structure around the drifted nodes by hill climbing with transfer learning (HC-TL), which is not implemented. Its ablation (Fig. 12) shows that detection is driven by the statistic, with equivalent results for the parameter and sliding updates.

References

Sojo, R., Bielza, C. and Larrañaga, P. (2027). A fully unsupervised concept drift detector via Bayesian networks for machine condition monitoring. Expert Systems with Applications, 332, 133634. doi:10.1016/j.eswa.2026.133634

See also

spbn()

Examples

library(daltoolbox)
library(heimdall)
set.seed(1)
n <- 3000
a <- stats::rnorm(n)
b <- a + stats::rnorm(n, sd = 0.5)
b[2001:n] <- b[2001:n] + 2
detector <- dfr_llr2(n_baseline = 1000, window_size = 200, step = 50)
model <- fit(detector, data.frame(a, b))
model$drifts
#> [[1]]
#> [[1]]$observation
#> [1] 2100
#> 
#> [[1]]$nodes
#> [1] "b"
#> 
#> [[1]]$lambda
#>        b 
#> -3.40449 
#> 
#> [[1]]$p_value
#>           b 
#> 0.009070055 
#> 
#>
